title: [TLS] BouncyCastle provider performs no certificate chain validation and weak hostname matching
body:
## Summary
`TurboTlsAuthentication.ValidateCertificateChain` is an empty TODO guarded by a `#warning`. The BouncyCastle TLS path accepts any certificate chain whose leaf has a matching hostname and valid dates, so any on-path attacker with a self-signed certificate can intercept traffic. Hostname matching is also non-compliant.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/TurboTlsAuthentication.cs:59-70` — `ValidateCertificateChain` only checks `chain.Length == 0`; `#warning "Phase 3C: Certificate chain validation is NOT implemented"`
- `Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/TurboTlsAuthentication.cs:151-171` — hostname / wildcard matching

## Problem
- No signature verification, no trust-anchor check, no basic constraints / key usage / EKU checks, no revocation.
- Wildcard handling lets `*.com` match `example.com`; CN is used even when a SAN extension is present; IP-address SANs are ignored.

Scenario: app runs with `TlsBackend.BouncyCastle` (or Auto falls back to it, see TLS-02). Attacker on Wi-Fi presents a self-signed cert for `api.example.com` with valid dates. Handshake succeeds; attacker reads/modifies all HTTPS traffic including `Authorization` headers.

## Spec reference
RFC 5280 §6 (certification path validation), RFC 6125 §6 (service identity: SAN-only when SAN present, wildcard only in left-most label, no partial/public-suffix wildcards), RFC 6066 §3.

## Suggested fix
1. Implement PKIX path validation (`PkixCertPathBuilder`/`PkixCertPathValidator` from the vendored BC lib) against platform roots (Android: system store via JNI or bundled Mozilla roots; iOS: bundled roots or SecTrust bridge), with EKU `serverAuth`, basic constraints, key usage.
2. Rewrite hostname matching per RFC 6125: SAN dNSName/iPAddress only when SAN present, single left-most wildcard label, reject wildcards spanning public suffix / TLD.
3. Add an optional user `ServerCertificateValidationCallback` hook consistent with the SslStream path.
4. Remove the `#warning` once done; until done, BC must be unreachable without explicit insecure opt-in (TLS-02).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Untrusted root, self-signed, expired, not-yet-valid, wrong-host, and `*.com` wildcard certs are rejected with `UHttpErrorType` certificate error
- [ ] Valid public chain (e.g. Let's Encrypt) succeeds on iOS and Android IL2CPP devices
- [ ] Negative TLS test suite runs against both SslStream and BouncyCastle providers
- [ ] `#warning` removed from `TurboTlsAuthentication.cs`

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [TLS] Auto mode silently and permanently falls back to unvalidated BouncyCastle; SslStream treats h2 as required whenever offered
body:
## Summary
In `TlsBackend.Auto`, a platform exception during the SslStream handshake calls `TlsProviderSelector.MarkSslStreamBroken()`, which switches the whole process to BouncyCastle for every later connection. Because the pool always offers `{"h2","http/1.1"}` and `SslStreamTlsProvider` treats any presence of `h2` as *required*, a runtime without SslStream ALPN throws `PlatformNotSupportedException` and triggers that fallback. Combined with TLS-01, every HTTPS connection becomes MITM-able by default on such runtimes.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Tls/SslStreamTlsProvider.cs:145-151` — `RequiresProtocol(alpnProtocols, "h2")` + `!_alpnSupported` → throws PNSE
- `Runtime/Transport/Tls/SslStreamTlsProvider.cs:337` — `RequiresProtocol` returns true if `h2` is anywhere in the list
- `Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:577` and `RawSocketTransport.cs:30` — always pass `{"h2","http/1.1"}`
- `Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:591-620` — Auto + `IsPlatformTlsException` (`NotSupportedException`, `TypeLoadException`, `FileNotFoundException`, PNSE) → `MarkSslStreamBroken()` and retry with BC
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:982` — CONNECT tunnels also follow the cached selection

## Problem
Trigger chain on an IL2CPP device where ALPN reflection members are unavailable/stripped:
1. First HTTPS request → SslStream path → PNSE (h2 "required").
2. Auto mode classifies PNSE as platform failure → `MarkSslStreamBroken()` (process-wide, never reset).
3. All subsequent connections, including CONNECT tunnels, use BouncyCastle, which does no chain validation (TLS-01).

Also: with `TlsBackend.SslStream` or Auto without BC, every HTTPS request fails instead of negotiating HTTP/1.1, contradicting the class doc at `SslStreamTlsProvider.cs:16-18`.

## Spec reference
RFC 7301 (ALPN is a negotiation; absence must fall back to http/1.1).

## Suggested fix
1. Treat `h2` as optional whenever `http/1.1` is also offered: if ALPN unavailable, do a plain handshake and report negotiated protocol = http/1.1.
2. Auto must fail closed: never fall back to a provider that does not perform full chain validation. Gate BC fallback behind TLS-01 being complete; until then require an explicit opt-in such as `TlsBackend.BouncyCastleInsecureForTesting`.
3. Make the broken-state cache resettable and per-reason; log once via `TlsProviderSelector.DiagnosticLogger`.
4. Document the selection matrix in platform docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Runtime without ALPN + Auto: HTTPS succeeds over SslStream HTTP/1.1, no BC fallback, no PNSE
- [ ] Auto never selects BouncyCastle while BC chain validation is unimplemented
- [ ] Unit test: simulated `_alpnSupported=false` with `{h2,http/1.1}` → plain TLS handshake, no exception
- [ ] Unit test: platform exception in Auto does not route to an unvalidated provider
- [ ] Device check on iOS/Android IL2CPP recorded in Phase 9 matrix

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [TLS] link.xml preserves SslStream types under the wrong assembly name for Unity
body:
## Summary
`Runtime/Transport/link.xml` preserves SslStream / ALPN types under assembly `System.Net.Security`, but on Unity Mono/IL2CPP these types live in `System.dll`. The rules are likely no-ops, so the reflection-based ALPN probe in `SslStreamTlsProvider` can be stripped at Medium/High managed stripping.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/link.xml` — `<assembly fullname="System.Net.Security">` entries
- `Runtime/Transport/Tls/SslStreamTlsProvider.cs` — reflection lookup of `SslClientAuthenticationOptions` / `SslApplicationProtocol` members

## Problem
With stripping enabled, ALPN members are removed → `_alpnSupported=false` → (before TLS-02 is fixed) PNSE and BouncyCastle fallback; after TLS-02, HTTP/2 silently never negotiates.

## Suggested fix
Preserve the types under `System` (and keep `System.Net.Security` entry for newer Unity profiles), or ship an `IUnityLinkerProcessor` that emits the correct rules (see packaging link.xml issue). Verify with a stripped IL2CPP build log.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] IL2CPP build with High stripping keeps ALPN members (verified via linker output or runtime probe log)
- [ ] HTTP/2 negotiates over SslStream on a device where the runtime supports ALPN

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Plausible (needs IL2CPP build confirmation).

title: [TLS] BouncyCastle TlsStream serialises reads and writes, stalling HTTP/2 and Expect: 100-continue
body:
## Summary
`BouncyCastleTlsProvider` returns the raw vendored `protocol.Stream`. Its async overrides forward to base `Stream.ReadAsync/WriteAsync(byte[])` → `BeginRead/BeginWrite`, which share a single semaphore in the BCL base implementation; a pending read blocks every write and occupies a thread-pool thread inside `ReadApplicationData`.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/BouncyCastleTlsProvider.cs:121-126` — returns `protocol.Stream` unwrapped
- Vendored `TlsStream` — only `ReadAsync(Memory)`/`WriteAsync(ReadOnlyMemory)` overridden

## Problem
- HTTP/2: the read loop always has a read outstanding, so HEADERS/DATA/SETTINGS-ACK writes wait until the server sends something → requests stall until timeout.
- HTTP/1.1 Expect: 100-continue timeout branch writes the body while `initialHeadTask` is reading → deadlock.
BouncyCastle is the designated IL2CPP HTTP/2 path, so this hits exactly the platforms it exists for.

## Suggested fix
Wrap the BC stream in a duplex adapter: independent read path (dedicated reader or overrides of `byte[]` async methods that bypass the base semaphore) and a lock-protected write path; or drive `TlsClientProtocol` in non-blocking mode with explicit socket I/O.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Concurrent read+write test over BouncyCastle: write completes while a read is pending (timeout-bounded)
- [ ] HTTP/2 over BouncyCastle: 50 concurrent requests complete against a real h2 server
- [ ] Expect: 100-continue timeout path completes over BouncyCastle
- [ ] Validated on iOS and Android IL2CPP devices

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Plausible (traced; depends on BCL base-Stream semantics, needs device test).

title: [HTTP/1.1] Expect: 100-continue early final response returns connection to pool with unsent body (request desync)
body:
## Summary
When a server answers an `Expect: 100-continue` request with a final status (401/413/417) before the declared body is sent, the head is returned with the server's keep-alive value and the connection goes back to the pool. The declared Content-Length/chunked body was never written, so a server that keeps reading the request body consumes the next pooled request as that body.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1605-1612, 1688-1692` — early final response path keeps `KeepAlive`
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:85-89, 683-686` — empty/HEAD body completes and calls `ReturnToPool()`
- `Tests/.../RawSocketTransportTests.cs` — `RawSocketTransport_ExpectContinue_KeepAliveRejectionWithBody_ReusesConnectionAfterDrain` asserts the buggy reuse (`AcceptCount == 1`)

## Problem
Client sends `POST /upload` with `Content-Length: 1000000` + `Expect: 100-continue`. Server replies `401` keep-alive and continues reading-and-discarding the declared body (allowed by RFC 9110 §10.1.1). Client returns the connection to the pool; next request `GET /me` + `Authorization: Bearer …` is consumed as body bytes of the first request. Responses then go to the wrong requests (desync) and credentials end up in the wrong request context.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §10.1.1 (server MAY keep reading and discarding content), RFC 9112 §9.6 / §9.3 (connection reuse requires complete message framing).

## Suggested fix
If a final response arrives while `!requestWriteState.HasCommittedBodyBytes` and the request declared a non-zero body, force `KeepAlive = false` and close after the response (matches SocketsHttpHandler). Optionally: if the body is small and replayable, finish sending it instead of closing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Early final response with unsent declared body never returns the connection to the pool
- [ ] Test `RawSocketTransport_ExpectContinue_KeepAliveRejectionWithBody_ReusesConnectionAfterDrain` flipped to assert a new connection (`AcceptCount == 2`)
- [ ] New test: server that reads-and-discards the declared body does not receive the next request as body
- [ ] Content-Length: 0 requests remain reusable

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [Transport] PollSelect socket mode busy-spins on idle connections
body:
## Summary
With `SocketIoMode.PollSelect`, `TryServiceRecv`/`TryServiceSend` return before calling `Poll` when nothing is pending, so the poll thread loops on `Thread.Sleep(0)` — a tight spin for every pooled connection.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Tcp/PollSelectSocketChannel.cs:156-168, 182, 250` — early returns before `Poll`
- `Runtime/Transport/Tcp/PollSelectSocketChannel.cs:276-281` — send-retry loop starves receive servicing

## Problem
Each idle pooled HTTP/1.1 connection burns close to a full core for up to the 2-minute idle timeout, multiplied by `maxConnectionsPerHost` → battery drain and thermal throttling on mobile. The send-retry loop also stops receives being serviced, which can deadlock full-duplex HTTP/2 (peer blocked on its own send window).

## Suggested fix
Block on a signal when nothing is pending (e.g. `SemaphoreSlim`/`ManualResetEventSlim` set by `ReceiveAsync`/`SendAsync`), and use a single `Socket.Select` over read+write interest, interleaving send-retry with receive servicing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Idle PollSelect connection consumes ~0% CPU (measured in a test or profiler capture)
- [ ] Full-duplex test: large concurrent send and receive on one PollSelect channel completes without deadlock
- [ ] Existing PollSelect tests still pass

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed (spin); deadlock Plausible.

title: [HTTP/1.1] EOF in the middle of response headers is accepted as a complete header block
body:
## Summary
At EOF, `ReadLineAsync` returns the partial line or an empty string. The header loop treats `""` as the blank line terminating headers, so a connection that closes mid-headers is accepted as a complete response.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:264-276` — `string.IsNullOrEmpty(line)` → break
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:1007-1014` — EOF handling in line reader
- `Http11ResponseParser.cs:825-827`, `Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:421-427` — same issue for trailers

## Problem
Server/attacker sends `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Le` then FIN. Client produces a successful 200 with no framing headers, reads body to close (empty), and the Cache interceptor may store the truncated response.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 §2.1, §8 (incomplete messages must be treated as errors when framing is incomplete).

## Suggested fix
Distinguish EOF from an empty line: return `null` on EOF, and throw `IOException`/`UHttpException(NetworkError)` if EOF occurs before the CRLF CRLF terminator or mid-line. Apply the same rule to the trailer section.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Truncated headers (EOF mid-line and EOF before blank line) raise a network error, not a response
- [ ] Truncated trailers raise an error
- [ ] Parser tests cover both cases for buffered and streaming paths

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Transfer-Encoding handling allows response smuggling and desync
body:
## Summary
Transfer-Encoding processing has four defects that allow framing confusion on reused connections.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:425-458` — TE / CL framing decision

## Problem
1. `headers.Get` reads only the first `Transfer-Encoding` field line: `TE: chunked` + `TE: gzip` is framed as chunked although the final coding is gzip.
2. `gzip, chunked` returns gzip bytes undecoded and unlabelled.
3. TE + Content-Length together is accepted and the connection is reused (only an event is recorded).
4. TE in an HTTP/1.0 response is not treated as faulty framing.

Result: response splitting / desync on reused connections behind misbehaving or malicious intermediaries.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 §6.1 (final coding must be chunked; TE+CL → MUST close after response; TE in HTTP/1.0 → faulty framing), §6.3.

## Suggested fix
Join all TE field values; require final coding == `chunked`, otherwise read to close; reject or surface unknown codings; when TE and CL both present ignore CL and set `KeepAlive = false`; treat TE in HTTP/1.0 responses as read-to-close with `KeepAlive = false`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Multi-line TE with non-chunked final coding is not parsed as chunked
- [ ] TE+CL response closes the connection after the response
- [ ] HTTP/1.0 + TE response is not reused
- [ ] Parser tests for each case

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [HTTP/1.1] obs-fold lines and whitespace before colon accepted as new header fields
body:
## Summary
Header lines starting with SP/HTAB (obs-fold) and `Name : value` (whitespace before colon) are trimmed and accepted as independent fields. Field names are not validated as tokens on the main path (only trailers are).

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:282` — `TryParseHeaderLine` call
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:591-605` — trimming / name parsing

## Problem
` Transfer-Encoding: chunked` or `Content-Length : 0` changes client framing in a way intermediaries would not → smuggling / response splitting surface.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 §5.1 (no whitespace between field name and colon — MUST reject), §5.2 (obs-fold: replace with SP or reject), §2.2; RFC 9110 §5.1 (field-name = token).

## Suggested fix
Reject whitespace before colon; either fold continuation lines into the previous value with SP or reject the response; validate names against tchar.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Name : value` rejected
- [ ] Leading-whitespace line folded or rejected (decided + documented)
- [ ] Non-token header names rejected
- [ ] Tests for each

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Stale pooled connection retry ignores EOF before status line
body:
## Summary
The stale-connection retry only fires for `IOException`/`SocketException`. The most common stale case — the server closed the idle connection (FIN/close_notify) between the `IsAlive` probe and the request — produces a 0-byte read and `FormatException("Empty HTTP status line")`, which is not retried.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:353-357, 710-714` — retry filter
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:265-266` — `FormatException("Empty HTTP status line")`

## Problem
User sees intermittent `Malformed HTTP response` errors after idle periods (server keep-alive timeout shorter than pool idle timeout).

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 §9.3.1 (retrying idempotent requests on closed persistent connections).

## Suggested fix
Include the existing `IsConnectionClosedBeforeStatusLine(ex)` in the retry filter for reused connections, keeping the idempotency / unsent-body rules.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reused connection closed before status line → transparent retry for idempotent requests
- [ ] Fresh connection with same failure still surfaces error
- [ ] Test with server that closes idle connection

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [HTTP/1.1] 101 Switching Protocols response returns upgraded connection to the pool
body:
## Summary
101 is treated as a final response with an empty body; `Connection: upgrade` has no `close` token so `KeepAlive` stays true and the switched-protocol connection is returned to the pool. The serializer lets user `Upgrade`/`Connection` headers through.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:243, 416-422` — 101 handling
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:85-89` — empty body → `ReturnToPool()`
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:319-336` — user `Upgrade`/`Connection` pass-through

## Problem
A request with `Upgrade: websocket` or `h2c` gets 101; the next pooled HTTP request is written into a WebSocket/h2c stream → garbage responses or desync.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §15.2.2, §7.8 (after 101 the connection speaks the new protocol).

## Suggested fix
Either reject `Upgrade` requests on the HTTP transport (WebSocket has its own transport), or force `KeepAlive = false` and never pool a connection after 101.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 101 response never returns connection to the pool
- [ ] Decision (reject vs close) documented
- [ ] Test covering 101 response

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [HTTP/1.1] CONNECT proxy reply line reader is unbounded; 2xx CONNECT body is drained
body:
## Summary
`ReadAsciiLineAsync` used for proxy CONNECT replies has no per-line cap; the 16 KB total is checked only after each line is complete, and the status line and chunk-size lines are not counted. A 2xx CONNECT reply's Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding is drained although they must be ignored.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1312-1364` — `ReadAsciiLineAsync`
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:978, 1143-1169` — CONNECT reply handling / drain

## Problem
- Malicious proxy (or MITM on the plaintext proxy leg) streams bytes with no LF → pooled buffer keeps doubling → OOM before the request timeout fires.
- Proxy returns `200` with non-zero `Content-Length` → client waits to drain bytes that never come → tunnel hangs.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §9.3.6 (client MUST ignore Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding in a 2xx CONNECT response).

## Suggested fix
Enforce a per-line cap (~8 KB) inside the read loop and count status line in the total; skip body drain for 2xx CONNECT responses.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Line without LF beyond cap fails fast with bounded memory
- [ ] 200 CONNECT with Content-Length establishes tunnel without draining
- [ ] Tests for both

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Expect-continue cancellation returns read buffer to pool while a read is pending
body:
## Summary
In the expect-continue path, on caller cancellation `timeoutTask` wins and `ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` throws; the `finally` returns the `BufferedStreamReader` buffer to the ArrayPool while `initialHeadTask` is still reading. The socket is only closed later by `lease.Dispose` in `DispatchCoreAsync`.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1596-1668, 1729-1734`

## Problem
Mono `NetworkStream`/`SslStream` do not honour the token mid-read, and PollSelect copies into the target after `Receive`. Late-arriving bytes are written into an array another renter now owns → memory corruption in an unrelated request.

## Suggested fix
Order the teardown: dispose the lease/socket first, then observe `initialHeadTask` (await/ignore exception), then dispose the reader and return buffers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Buffer return happens only after the pending read has completed/faulted
- [ ] Stress test: cancel during expect-continue wait with delayed server bytes, no cross-request corruption

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Plausible.

title: [TLS] Host header and SNI use Uri.Host instead of IdnHost; IP literals sent in SNI
body:
## Summary
Host header, SNI and authority use `Uri.Host` (Unicode form under IRI parsing) instead of `Uri.IdnHost`. BouncyCastle also sends IP literals (with IPv6 brackets) in SNI.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:290-316` — Host header
- `Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/TurboTlsClient.cs:62-67` — SNI server name

## Problem
- CJK hosts throw `ArgumentException` from `GetLatin1Bytes`.
- `münchen.de` sent as raw 0xFC byte in Host.
- BC sends Unicode label as UTF-8 in SNI and sends IP literals in SNI → strict servers abort the handshake.

## Spec reference
RFC 6066 §3 (HostName is ASCII A-label; literal IPv4/IPv6 addresses are not permitted), RFC 9110 §7.2, RFC 3987 / IDNA 2008.

## Suggested fix
Use `Uri.IdnHost` for Host, `:authority`, SNI and certificate name matching; skip SNI for IP literals; strip brackets from the TLS target host.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] IDN host produces punycode Host and SNI
- [ ] IP-literal hosts send no SNI on both providers
- [ ] Tests for IDN and IPv4/IPv6 literals

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Plausible.

title: [Transport] No TCP keepalive and long idle timeout cause half-dead connection reuse on mobile
body:
## Summary
`SO_KEEPALIVE` is never set and pooled connections idle up to 2 minutes. Mobile NATs silently drop idle mappings; `IsAlive` still passes (no FIN), the write succeeds into the kernel buffer and the read hangs for the full request timeout.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:543-566` — socket setup / idle timeout
- `Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:353-356` — socket options

## Problem
After a few idle minutes on cellular, the first request reuses a dead connection and fails with Timeout (not retried by the stale-connection path).

## Suggested fix
Enable `SO_KEEPALIVE` (with platform keepalive intervals where available), shorten default idle timeout on mobile (e.g. 30–60 s), and/or add a short first-byte timeout for reused connections that triggers a transparent retry for idempotent requests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Keepalive enabled on pooled sockets
- [ ] Mobile default idle timeout documented and reduced
- [ ] Reused-connection first-byte timeout retries idempotent requests (test with blackholed server)

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Plausible.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Bodiless non-idempotent request is auto-replayed after it was fully sent
body:
## Summary
`HasCommittedBodyBytes` is always false for requests with no body, so a bodiless POST/PATCH that was fully written on a reused connection and then hit an IOException (RST after the server processed it) is replayed automatically.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:159-168` — stale retry decision
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:177, 250` — commit tracking

## Problem
Server processes `POST /purchase` (no body), connection reset before response → client replays → duplicate side effect.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §9.2.2 (non-idempotent requests must not be automatically retried unless known not processed).

## Suggested fix
Track a `RequestHeadFullyWritten` flag; do not auto-retry non-idempotent requests once the head has been fully written.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Non-idempotent bodiless request is not replayed after full head write
- [ ] Idempotent requests still retried
- [ ] Test with server that resets after reading request

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Header and trailer values allow NUL and other control characters
body:
## Summary
Request header and trailer value validation rejects only CR and LF. NUL and other CTLs pass through; some servers/intermediaries truncate at NUL or treat CTLs differently.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:514-528`

## Problem
User-influenced header value containing `\0` is truncated differently by front-end and back-end → header confusion.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 §5.5 (field values: VCHAR / obs-text / SP / HTAB; NUL MUST be rejected or replaced).

## Suggested fix
Reject 0x00–0x08, 0x0A–0x1F and 0x7F in field values (HTAB allowed); share the validator with HTTP/2 request header validation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Values with NUL/CTL rejected with clear error
- [ ] Shared validator used by HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
- [ ] Tests

## Context
Source: 2026-10 full review (`Development/docs/review-2026-10-full-library-review.md`). Confidence: Confirmed.
